projectBaseline.identityStatus: identityEstablished=false; implementationCapabilities=Not yet implemented or verified; consumerIntegration=Not yet established
projectBaseline.implementationObservation: The GPWCF project entry-point Python file is empty and requirements.txt states that the current framework baseline uses the Python standard library only. The inspected project contains architecture contracts but no executable Stage/Step/SPU runtime implementation classes.
projectBaseline.interpretation: PHASE-01 is therefore a Prefect native-capability qualification using explicitly labelled contract-shaped fixtures. It is not evidence of real GPWCF production-class binding.

contracts.relevantContract: Stage owns its Step composition and exposes a Stage facade to the consuming workflow; no concrete Python class or fixed callable signature is prescribed.
execute(input: TInput) -> StepExecutionResult[TOutput]. Stage interacts only through this public Step boundary and must not invoke internal SPUs or Supporting Units directly.

Concrete Step owns Step Composition; it defines internal component selection, transition semantics, execution evidence and result assembly. No universal StepComposition callable signature or separate runtime object is mandated.
Step Composition invokes specialized StepProcessingUnit[TInput,TOutput] instances; SPUs do not own Step flow control.
SPUExecutionResult[TOutput] is the normally returned per-SPU result; it is not StepExecutionResult and does not own Step aggregation.

StepExecutionResult[TOutput] is assembled by the Step/Step Composition and exposes independently optional processingArtifact, validatorResult, errorResult and errorHandlerResult. No universal success boolean is introduced.

pipelineRoot.authority: Prefect owns the native Root Flow and pipeline-level orchestration.
pipelineRoot.gpwcfContract: No separate concrete GPWCF Root callable contract was identified in the inspected project documents.
pipelineRoot.phase01Shape: A PoC Root Flow invokes multiple Stage Parent Flows and passes explicit invocation correlation.

stage.authority: Stage specialization owns Stage-facing behavior and its Step membership/flow semantics; Prefect executes the native Stage Parent Flow.
stage.callableStatus: The Stage facade is specified as an architectural role; concrete Python callable/class shape remains to be implemented or specialized.

step.authority: Concrete Step owns the public execute contract and Step Composition semantics.
step.callableStatus: The generic execute signature and StepExecutionResult return type are specified; concrete Step implementations and concrete TInput/TOutput specializations are not yet present in the GPWCF Python package.

spu.authority: Concrete SPU owns its specialized processing behavior and SPUExecutionResult.
spu.callableStatus: Generic SPU callable/result contracts are documented; no production SPU Python classes are currently present.

referenceConsumer.decompositionRule: Stage Model objectives and execution_steps are not presumed to be GPWCF Steps or SPUs. Concrete Step/SPU instances must be derived from the specialized Stage and Step contracts before PHASE-03/04 production binding.

identityAndResultRules: Pipeline, Stage, Step and SPU domain identities remain separate from Prefect Flow Run and Task Run IDs.
Prefect State is operational execution evidence, not a domain result.
SPUExecutionResult and StepExecutionResult remain distinct types and assembly boundaries.
A Step Flow is invoked only through the public Step.execute facade from its owning Stage.
Stage Flow code does not call Step-owned SPU or Supporting Unit Tasks directly.
Supporting Unit patterns are excluded from this PHASE-01 minimal vertical slice; no generic Supporting Unit runtime is introduced.
